title: Universal signed shuffle and its natural homotopy inverse
statement:
Let $I=\Delta	imes\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is the category of nonempty finite ordinals and monotone maps, and let $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathrm{Ab})$. For $i\in I$ set $R_i(j)=\mathbf Z[\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)]$, with postcomposition maps. Let $P_n=R_{(n,n)}$ and $Q_n= igoplus_{a+b=n}R_{(a,b)}$, with diagonal and separately signed alternating-deletion boundaries and vertex-sum augmentations $\epsilon_P,\epsilon_Q$ to $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, as in [lem-sfb-free-bisimplex-projective-resolutions].

For $a+b=n$ and a partition $\mu\sqcup
u=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with $|\mu|=a$, $|
u|=b$, let $\alpha_\mu:[n]	o[a]$ send $k$ to $\#\{j\in\mu:j<k\}$, and define $\alpha_
u$ likewise. Let $\epsilon(\mu,
u)$ be the sign of the permutation listing $\mu$ then $
u$, each increasingly. Define $\sigma_n:Q_n	o P_n$ on the distinguished generator of its $R_{(a,b)}$ summand, at $(a,b)$, by
$$[1_{(a,b)}]\longmapsto\sum_{\mu,
u}\epsilon(\mu,
u)[(\alpha_\mu,\alpha_
u)]\in R_{(n,n)}(a,b),$$
and extend by postcomposition and integral linearity at every object of $I$. Then $\sigma$ is a natural chain map and $\epsilon_P\sigma_0=\epsilon_Q$. There exist a natural chain map $	au:P	o Q$ with $\epsilon_Q	au_0=\epsilon_P$ and natural degree-raising maps $h_P:P_n	o P_{n+1}$, $h_Q:Q_n	o Q_{n+1}$ such that
$$\sigma	au-1_P=\partial_Ph_P+h_P\partial_P,\qquad 	au\sigma-1_Q=\partial_Qh_Q+h_Q\partial_Q.$$
Thus this prescribed $\sigma$, not merely a chosen comparison map, is a chain homotopy equivalence, and its class is an isomorphism $Q\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ in $D(\mathcal E)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], placing the chain degree $n$ in cochain degree $-n$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-free-bisimplex-projective-resolutions], $\mathcal E$ is abelian and $P,Q$ are projective resolutions of $\underline{\mathbf Z}$. Its generator bijection extends each specified finite sum uniquely to a morphism $R_{(a,b)}\to P_n$. For $t:(p,q)\to(p',q')$, postcomposition takes each basis arrow $s$ to $ts$, so both orders of applying $t$ and this extension give the same shuffle sum. Thus each $\sigma_n$ is a morphism of diagrams.

proof.text: Evaluate at $(p,q)$. The identifications $P(p,q)=V(p,q)$ and $Q(p,q)=\operatorname{Tot}(U(p)\otimes U(q))$ of [lem-sfb-free-bisimplex-projective-resolutions] send a basis arrow $(u,v):(a,b)\to(p,q)$ to its two strings. Its image under the prescribed map has $k$th vertex $(u_{\alpha_\mu(k)},v_{\alpha_\nu(k)})$. This is exactly the sum in [lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary], with the same partition sign. Its boundary and augmentation identities therefore give $\partial_P\sigma=\sigma\partial_Q$ and $\epsilon_P\sigma_0=\epsilon_Q$ at every object, hence in $\mathcal E$. This includes $a=0$, $b=0$, and repeated entries.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-projective-resolution-lift] in $\mathcal E$ to $f=1_{\underline{\mathbf Z}}$ and the ordered pair $(P,Q)$. These are precisely the projective resolutions supplied by [lem-sfb-free-bisimplex-projective-resolutions]. It gives a chain map $\tau:P\to Q$ with $\epsilon_Q\tau_0=\epsilon_P$. Since this lifting takes place in the functor category, all its components are natural in $(p,q)$.

source.place: Tags 0649 (lemma-morphisms-lift-projective) and 064A (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy-projective), with the prescribed combinatorial shuffle of lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary. Agent-formulated specialization; returned proof steps 4–5.

proof.text: The equalities $\epsilon_P\sigma_0\tau_0=\epsilon_Q\tau_0=\epsilon_P$ and $\epsilon_Q\tau_0\sigma_0=\epsilon_P\sigma_0=\epsilon_Q$ show that $\sigma\tau$ and $1_P$, respectively $\tau\sigma$ and $1_Q$, have equal augmented composites. Apply [new-t4-augmented-resolution-lift-homotopy] first with source and target $P$, then with source and target $Q$. Their augmented exactness and projectivity were supplied in step 1. The resulting homotopies in $\mathcal E$ are natural degree-raising maps and give exactly the two displayed equations (the component in degree $-1$ is zero).

source.place: Tags 0649 (lemma-morphisms-lift-projective) and 064A (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy-projective), with the prescribed combinatorial shuffle of lem-sfb-simplex-lattice-shuffle-boundary. Agent-formulated specialization; returned proof steps 4–5.

proof.text: Put chain degree $n$ in cochain degree $-n$ and extend by zero in positive degrees. The two equations make the classes of $\sigma$ and $\tau$ inverse in the homotopy category. The localization from this category defining $D(\mathcal E)$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserves their two identity composites. Hence the class of this prescribed $\sigma$ is the asserted derived isomorphism.

Statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are unchanged from the Q23 creation; only the proof was added. Step 1: free-bisimplex gives an abelian E, the Yoneda bijection and projective resolutions, so σ is natural by Yoneda. Step 2: by naturality, σ sends the basis arrow (u,v) to Σε[(u∘α_μ, v∘α_ν)]. This is exactly the σ of lattice-shuffle-boundary (k-th vertex (u_{A_k},v_{B_k}), μ listed before ν, sign (−1)^a matching Q's boundary), so ∂_Pσ=σ∂_Q and ε_Pσ_0=ε_Q hold, including a=0, b=0 and repeated vertices. Small cases: n=0 gives σ_0=id; (1,1) gives the two paths with signs ±1. Step 3: the new leaf with A=E, f=1 and source P gives a natural τ with ε_Qτ_0=ε_P. Step 4: new-t4's hypotheses hold, applied once with K=P and once with K=Q; the augmentation identities are computed in the step and the homotopies live in E. Step 5: def-weil-abstract-derived-category gives D(A) as a localization of K(A), so this is elementary and yields a derived-form isomorphism. New node lem-sfb-abelian-projective-resolution-lift: a sound Mathlib leaf. ProjectiveResolution.lift is at Resolution.lean:92 and lift_commutes_zero at :106, needing only [Abelian C]. Its source Stacks 0649(2) (derived.tex:6777) applies because the augmentation is surjective in every degree. The node passes B1–B9. It is not a duplicate: the existing lift nodes cover modules only, new-t4 gives uniqueness only, and lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists is the dual statement.
